input: Apply to a local community radio station show

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Whether the user wants to pitch a brand-new show concept, apply for an existing open slot, or join as a contributor/guest changes the entire application approach.
Knowing whether this is a solo application or involves co-hosts/a team affects how to present the pitch and who needs to be coordinated.
The specific station or stations they are targeting determines the application format, requirements, and tone expected.
Knowing their availability (days, hours per week) is a hard limit that shapes what kind of show slot is realistic to apply for.
The genre or topic of the show they want to do is central to crafting a compelling, specific pitch.
Understanding whether the user's goal is just to submit an application, land an interview, or actually get on air helps define what 'done well' looks like and how much effort to invest.
Knowing what materials they already have (demo reel, bio, show outline) versus what still needs to be created determines the immediate next action.

gold.taskTitle: Apply to a local community radio show
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to apply to host or participate in a show at a local community radio station.

questions.title: Are you pitching a new show or applying for an existing slot?
questions.description: Clarifies whether the user needs to develop an original concept or respond to an open call with defined requirements.

questions.title: Will you be hosting solo or with co-hosts?
questions.description: Determines whether the application needs to represent a team and coordinate multiple people's availability and bios.

questions.title: Do you have a specific station in mind already?
questions.description: Identifies whether research into target stations is still needed or if the user is ready to apply to a known station.

questions.title: How many hours per week can you commit to the show?
questions.description: Establishes a hard availability constraint that shapes which show formats and time slots are realistic to apply for.

questions.title: What topic or genre do you want your show to cover?
questions.description: The show's subject matter is the core of any pitch and must be defined before application materials can be drafted.

questions.title: What does success look like — submitting, interviewing, or getting on air?
questions.description: Distinguishes between the immediate deliverable (a submitted application) and the broader goal (actually broadcasting), which affects how much preparation is warranted.

questions.title: What application materials do you already have ready?
questions.description: Determines what still needs to be created (demo audio, show outline, presenter bio) so the immediate next step can be identified.
